workflows.title: 00 Start here: triage queue
workflows.description: Work leads top to bottom. Red means there is something to work. Click the blue name to open its workflow.
intro:
## Start here
1. Work the leads **top to bottom**. They are ordered by how often they turn out to be the start of an intrusion.
2. A **red number** means the lead has something to work. Green means skip it.
3. In the lead's table, **click the blue value**. It opens the workflow for that lead with the user, host or asset filled in.
4. Each workflow ends with a **Decide** step that tells you whether to escalate and which workflow comes next. Add every user, host and IP you touch to the **case timeline**.

_Synthetic data. A scripted intrusion replays at the top of every UTC hour over about 30 minutes._

leads.title: Suspicious sign-in

evidence.title: Denied MFA pushes by user (click the user)

leads.why: Repeated MFA prompts the user did not start (MFA fatigue) are how a sprayed password becomes a working session.

leads.title: Endpoint detection that was not blocked

evidence.title: Hosts with allowed high/critical detections
evidence.expr: count(sum by (host) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | event_type="Detection" | severity=~"high|critical" | action="allowed" [$__range])))

evidence.title: Allowed high/critical detections (click the host)
evidence.expr: topk(20, sum by (host, user, detection_name) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | event_type="Detection" | severity=~"high|critical" | action="allowed" [$__range])))

leads.why: High and critical EDR detections where the action was *allowed* ran to completion. Someone has to look.

leads.title: Credential theft and lateral movement

evidence.title: RC4 service tickets by source host (click the host)
evidence.expr: sum by (src_host, user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | event_id="4769" | ticket_encryption="0x17" [$__range]))

leads.why: RC4 Kerberos service tickets (0x17). The fleet is AES-only, so RC4 requests mean someone is Kerberoasting service accounts.
leads.work_in: WF3 Lateral movement and privilege escalation

leads.title: Large upload to file sharing

evidence.title: Users over 100 MB
evidence.expr: count(sum by (user) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range])) > 100000000)

evidence.title: Uploads to file sharing over 100 MB (click the user)
evidence.expr: sum by (user, host, url_domain) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range])) > 100000000

leads.why: Over 100 MB to a personal file-sharing site from a corporate host. Vehicle program data is the crown jewel here.

leads.title: Unticketed change on the plant floor

evidence.title: Unticketed controller changes by asset (click the asset)
evidence.expr: sum by (site, asset, event_type) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | change_ticket="" | event_type=~"program_download|controller_mode_change|write_request" [$__range]))

leads.why: A program download, mode change or setpoint write with no change ticket. This can stop a line or hurt someone.

leads.title: Vehicle API key abuse

evidence.title: 404s by API key, all keys (click the key)

leads.why: Hundreds of 404s on one key means someone is guessing VINs. A hit returns a customer's car location.

workflows.title: Case timeline
workflows.description: Every source for one entity, in time order. Use it to write the case narrative.
intro: **How to use:** put one value in the Entity box (a user, host, IP, asset or file hash). Read the log **oldest first** and write one line per event in the case: time, source, what happened. Do this for every entity on your containment list. The first event across all of them is your initial access time.
